routes.description: Establish that the identified facts concerning contingent existence, the universe's beginning, fine-tuning, objective morality, and Jesus's resurrection collectively provide evidential support for God's existence.
routes.successCriteria: Show that each principal fact is more expected or better explained under the relevant theistic hypothesis than under the naturalistic alternatives presented, and connect the cumulative case to the God named in the motion.

motionBridge.description: The cited facts must collectively increase the probability of God's existence relative to the relevant alternatives.

centralBridges.description: Contingency and a finite cosmic past must warrant a necessary transcendent cause rather than an unexplained universe or solely physical origin.
Life-permitting conditions must be better explained by purposive design than by necessity, chance, dynamical mechanisms, or observer selection.
Objective moral values or duties must exist and require an ontological ground supplied by God's necessary moral character.
The relevant historical facts must be better explained by divine resurrection than by ordinary alternatives and must thereby support God's existence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Incremental probabilistic support must qualify as evidence without requiring proof or resolution of every prior-probability question.
The creator, designer, necessary being, and moral ground supported by the general arguments must connect coherently with the God identified through the resurrection claim.

routes.description: Show that the proffered facts do not establish evidential support for God because the hypothesis lacks adequate empirical discrimination, natural alternatives remain available, and the historical and moral inferences are underdetermined.
routes.successCriteria: Demonstrate that indispensable premises or inferential links in the cumulative case remain unsupported, that relevant observations are compatible with physical or ordinary explanations, or that generic theism fails to generate discriminating expectations.

motionBridge.description: The affirmative considerations must fail to provide sufficiently discriminating evidence for God over available naturalistic or ordinary alternatives.

centralBridges.description: Quantum cosmology, multiverse models, or unresolved physical explanation must block the inference from contingency or cosmic origins to a supernatural cause.
Dynamical explanations, multiverse variation, and anthropic selection must remain viable alternatives to a purposive designer.
Moral judgment or objective morality must remain intelligible without divine grounding, while conflicting religious judgments limit appeals to divine commands.
The resurrection reports must remain less warranted than error, invention, or other ordinary explanations given their documentation and background implausibility.

subsidiaryBridges.description: A God hypothesis must yield testable or discriminating expectations rather than accommodate any possible observation.
Unresolved scientific questions must motivate further physical investigation rather than function by themselves as positive evidence for God.

sections.title: Evidential Standard and Cumulative Burden
sections.rationale: The motion turns on what counts as evidence, whether incremental probability is sufficient, how priors and falsifiability matter, and how the separate considerations combine into a motion-level case.

sections.title: Contingency, Cosmic Beginning, and First Cause
sections.rationale: This issue combines the explanatory demand for contingent reality with disputes over actual infinity, a finite past, quantum origins, physical nothingness, and the inference to a transcendent cause.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Multiverse, and Design
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether life-permitting conditions favor purposive design or are accounted for by necessity, dynamics, multiverse variation, chance, or anthropic observer selection.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Its Ground
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether objective values and duties exist, whether naturalism can sustain them, and whether divine character provides a necessary and nonarbitrary foundation.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and Identification of God
sections.rationale: This issue covers the claimed historical facts, competing ordinary and miraculous explanations, testimonial standards, and the bridge from generic monotheism to the God associated with Jesus.
